text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- New decree gives Head of State, General Sani Abacha, the power to dissolve newly-elected local governments.
- Government bans sale of fuel in jerry-cans and instructs soldiers to escort fuel tankers as part of efforts to address the persistent fuel shortage.
- Nigeria has earned 5.5 billion naira from Value Added Tax in the first two months of 1997 compared to 4.4 billion naira in the same period of last year.

- National Insurance Company of Nigeria calls on appeal court to dismiss an application for a stay of execution on an order compelling it to insure the assets of Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation.
- Abacha orders release of national fuel reserves to cope with the current fuel scarcity.

- Manufacturers association president, Rufus Giwa, says more British investment could be brought to Nigeria if infrastructures were improved and if Nigerian visas were more easily available in Britain.
- Federal government has approved the installation of Instrument Landing Systems at all Nigeria's airports to improve their safety.
- Top officials of Fleming Martin, a South African finance firm, are in Nigeria to look at investment opportunities.
